groups.title: Direct, causative, and applicative object functions
groups.proposal: Keep direct, causative, and applicative objects morphologically alike but structurally distinct by linking each object to its lexical directive stem or causative/applicative suffix; admit open Sources and preserve the documented causative-shaped intransitive exception as a typed Source analysis rather than a stem whitelist.
groups.writingJob: Build each object as a typed governor unit, derive direct function from a directive Source and causative or applicative function from the selected derivational operation, require the corresponding object when the operation requires one, and allow a user-supplied exceptional intransitive analysis without treating the Canvas example as a gate.
groups.readingJob: Explain the three functions, show the causative object's two roles and the applicative object's indirect involvement, preserve translation and derivational-history uncertainty, and present the bathing example as evidence and a known exception rather than a closed lexical list.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the open Source, its valence analysis, each intended participant, and the causative or applicative operation. Object function and the discontinuous object-plus-suffix relation are automatic when that history fixes them; a role or exceptional intransitive analysis is exposed only when the intended Source analysis is genuinely unresolved.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source, Valence, Derivation, object participant, and conditional Reading or Source-analysis controls; do not add direct-versus-causative-versus-applicative, two-role, indirect-benefit, suffix-support, translation, or Canvas-example switches.

groups.title: Multiple Valence positions and the three-position ceiling
groups.proposal: Derive zero, one, two, or three complete Valence positions from the open Source and its ordered causative or applicative history, with an absolute maximum of three and no user-entered slot count.
groups.writingJob: Start from the typed intransitive or directive Source, add one complete Valence position for each participant-adding derivational operation, preserve the original directive object when present, and block a fourth position.
groups.readingJob: Show why derivation creates double- and triple-object VNCs, identify the intransitive-source and directive-source histories, and explain that every va is a complete Valence position rather than a printed placeholder.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the Source, each real derivational operation, and its participant. The application derives source-history type, position count, completeness, and the three-position ceiling.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source, Valence, Derivation, and participant controls; do not add object-count, double-versus-triple, history-schema, va-completeness, or maximum-position controls.

groups.title: Intransitive-source one-, two-, and three-object histories
groups.proposal: Build an intransitive Source with no object, then let one, two, or three ordered causative/applicative operations add one mainline object at a time while automatically relegating every earlier object to its correct shuntline level.
groups.writingJob: Preserve the objectless intransitive base, require contiguous derivational levels, add exactly one governed object per causative or applicative operation, make the last-added object mainline, and retain earlier objects as first- or second-level shuntline participants.
groups.readingJob: Trace the IBASE-SUF history through the one-, two-, and three-object schemas and show which object is mainline or shuntline without confusing derivational history with surface order.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses each causative or applicative operation and supplies its participant. The application assigns levels, mainline or shuntline status, and object count automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse recursive Derivation and participant controls; do not add one/two/three-object, derivational-level, mainline, shuntline, earlier-level, or later-level controls.

groups.title: Directive-source one-, two-, and three-object histories
groups.proposal: Retain the directive Source's direct object at level one, then add causative or applicative objects in contiguous levels, automatically shunting earlier objects and allowing a third causative layer only when the supplied Source meaning supports that rare history.
groups.writingJob: Bind the original direct object to the directive Source, add one governed object per later operation, preserve contiguous history and correct prominence, and require explicit Source meaning support for the extremely limited third causative stage.
groups.readingJob: Trace DBASE through one-, two-, and three-object histories, distinguish first- and second-level shuntline objects, and keep history separate from later linear ordering.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the directive Source, direct object, later operations, and their participants; a rare third causative history requires a genuine Source-analysis choice. The application derives all levels and prominence.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source, Valence, Derivation, participant, and conditional Source-analysis controls; do not add direct-object level, mainline, shuntline, or rarity switches.

groups.title: Filled Valence positions and the single mainline reflexive
groups.proposal: Require every Valence position and subposition to remain present even when silent, permit only one mainline reflexive shape, and normally bind that mainline reflexive to the last-added derivational operation.
groups.writingJob: Keep silent positions structurally present, enforce one mainline reflexive, and derive its control from the last-added suffix except where a later accepted rule supplies a documented exception.
groups.readingJob: Show silent structural positions, mainline reflexive shape, suffix control, and the later exception references without applying those later exceptions prematurely.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses reflexive participation only where semantically intended. Position presence, mainline count, carrier shape, and normal suffix control are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse object interpretation and participant controls; do not add fill-silent-position, mainline-reflexive, suffix-control, or rare-exception switches.

groups.title: Suffix order, object prominence, and incompatible specific objects
groups.proposal: Preserve the chosen causative/applicative suffix history, normally place causative before applicative, derive object prominence from history but surface object order from form, and keep all incompatible specific objects structurally present while sounding only one.
groups.writingJob: Validate the ordered suffix history, allow an exceptional suffix order only when specifically authorized, derive mainline and shuntline roles, and automatically silence incompatible specific objects without deleting them.
groups.readingJob: Contrast suffix-history order with object-pronoun order and show every sounded or silent specific participant and its continued grammatical reality.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended derivational operations and any genuinely documented exceptional order. The application derives prominence, surface ordering jurisdiction, and specific-object silencing.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Derivation and participant controls with a conditional order choice only for a real alternative; do not add prominence, surface-order, incompatibility, sound, or delete-object controls.

groups.title: Multiple-Valence formula, mainline privilege, and silent shuntline objects
groups.proposal: Project every complete Valence position into the shared multiple-object formula, privilege the last-added mainline object, silence only the incompatible specific shuntline carrier required by the stated person and number rules, and realize nonspecific and shuntline reflexive carriers automatically.
groups.writingJob: Build the full typed formula from the object cluster, retain every position, choose the one sounded specific object by mainline privilege, derive the correct silent dyad or subposition, preserve tē and tla, and realize shuntline reflexive or reciprocal ne.
groups.readingJob: Expose the formula's complete positions, mainline and shuntline structure, every silent participant, the person-sensitive silent carrier, and the distinction between derivational and nonspecific tla.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies participants through Source and derivational composition. Formula layout, prominence, incompatibility, silencing, tē, tla, and ne are automatic consequences.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source, Derivation, and participant controls; do not add formula-line, mainline, shuntline, sounded-object, silent-dyad, subposition, tē, tla, or ne controls.

groups.title: Object-pronoun order, thirteen combinations, and role ambiguity
groups.proposal: Order object carriers universally by form—specific before reflexive, specific before nonspecific, reflexive before nonspecific, and human before nonhuman—derive all valid two- and three-carrier sequences, integrate directional position, and preserve genuine direct/causative/applicative role ambiguity without changing the surface.
groups.writingJob: Sort the typed object cluster by the four priorities, derive the thirteen full combinations and valid subsequences, place directional material through the existing Lesson 8 rule, realize shuntline ne and silence, and keep governor-role assignments separate from carrier order.
groups.readingJob: Show form-based order, hidden participants, rare combinations, direction placement, the role of every carrier, and unresolved role mappings such as nēchtētla until context or the user's intended composition supplies them.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies participants and derivational governors; when several governor-role mappings genuinely yield the same carrier sequence, the user may choose the intended mapping or leave it open for reading. The application always derives carrier order and surface form.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse participant, Derivation, Direction, and conditional Reading or role-mapping controls; do not add ordering-priority, chart-row, two-versus-three, column, shuntline-ne, or silence switches.
